faqs.q: How much does a Field Spaniel cost to buy?
faqs.a: Reputable breeders typically charge $800–$3,000 for a Field Spaniel puppy. Prices vary by breeder reputation, health testing, and lineage. Rescue adoption fees are typically $100–$500 and include vaccinations, neutering, and microchipping.

faqs.q: What is the monthly cost of owning a Field Spaniel?
faqs.a: Budget $150–$300 per month for a Field Spaniel, covering food, preventive vet care, insurance, grooming and supplies. Mid-size breeds sit in the moderate cost range across most ownership categories.

faqs.q: What are the biggest ongoing costs for a Field Spaniel?
faqs.a: The three largest annual expenses are food ($500–900), veterinary care ($400–$1,200 budgeted annually), and pet insurance ($$400–$1,200 per year). Grooming adds $400–$1,200 annually for Field Spaniels due to their coat type.

faqs.q: How much does a Field Spaniel cost in the first year?
faqs.a: Year one costs for a Field Spaniel are significantly higher than subsequent years, typically $2,000–$4,000. This covers the purchase price or adoption fee, initial vet checks, vaccinations, spay/neuter, microchipping, crate, bedding, collar, leads and puppy training classes.

faqs.q: How often should I groom a Field Spaniel?
faqs.a: Field Spaniels need brushing 3–5 times per week, daily during seasonal coat blows.  Nails should be trimmed every 3–4 weeks. Ears should be checked and cleaned monthly.

faqs.q: Do Field Spaniels shed a lot?
faqs.a: Yes — they are considered heavy shedders. Regular brushing is the most effective control tool. A slicker brush and undercoat rake are both essential for Field Spaniels. Deshedding treatments from professional groomers can reduce seasonal shedding temporarily.

faqs.q: What grooming tools does a Field Spaniel need?
faqs.a: A slicker brush for surface debris and an undercoat rake for the dense undercoat are both essential. A shedding blade or deshedding tool helps during heavy moult periods. A nail grinder is useful if your Field Spaniel is sensitive to clippers.

faqs.q: How often should I bathe a Field Spaniel?
faqs.a: Every 4–6 weeks is appropriate for most Field Spaniels that live indoors. More frequent bathing is needed if they swim or spend time in mud. Over-bathing strips natural skin oils — use a pH-balanced dog shampoo rather than human products.

faqs.q: Are Field Spaniels easy to train?
faqs.a: Field Spaniels are considered easier to train than average — they respond quickly to reward-based methods and generalise cues well. Short 10–15 minute sessions outperform long correction-heavy drills.

faqs.q: What training method works best for a Field Spaniel?
faqs.a: Reward-based training using treats, praise and toy rewards is the most effective and well-researched approach for Field Spaniels. Keep sessions short and positive, end on a success, and vary your rewards to maintain engagement.

faqs.q: At what age should I start training my Field Spaniel?
faqs.a: Start training from the day your puppy arrives home, typically at 8 weeks. The 8–16 week window is the most sensitive socialisation period. Enrol in a puppy class within the first two weeks for structured socialisation alongside basic obedience foundations.

faqs.q: How long does it take to train a Field Spaniel?
faqs.a: Most Field Spaniels learn basic obedience cues (sit, stay, come, down) within 2–4 weeks of daily practice. Reliable recall in distracting environments typically takes 2–3 months of consistent reinforcement.

faqs.q: What health problems do Field Spaniels commonly have?
faqs.a: Field Spaniels are most commonly associated with hip dysplasia. Regular vet checks, appropriate weight management, and breed-specific screening tests help detect issues early. Ask any breeder for health test results before purchasing.

faqs.q: How long do Field Spaniels live?
faqs.a: Field Spaniels have an average lifespan of 12–13 years. Good nutrition, appropriate exercise, weight management and regular vet visits are the key factors in achieving the upper end of this range.

faqs.q: Are Field Spaniels prone to hip dysplasia?
faqs.a: Field Spaniels have a moderate-to-elevated risk of hip dysplasia, particularly for large or active breeds. Ask for OFA or PennHIP hip evaluation certificates when buying from a breeder. Weight control and avoiding high-impact exercise during bone growth (under 18 months) reduces risk.

faqs.q: What health tests should a Field Spaniel puppy have?
faqs.a: At minimum, your Field Spaniel puppy should have a vet health check, first vaccinations, deworming, and microchipping before coming home. Ask the breeder for parent health certificates relevant to Field Spaniel-specific conditions. A vet check within 72 hours of bringing your puppy home is recommended to establish a baseline.

faqs.q: Are Field Spaniels good with kids?
faqs.a: Field Spaniels are generally known for being friendly and patient, making them well-suited to family life with children. Supervision is always recommended with young children regardless of breed — interactions should be taught from both sides.

faqs.q: Do Field Spaniels get along with other dogs?
faqs.a: Field Spaniels are generally sociable with other dogs, particularly when well-socialised from puppyhood. Introduce new dogs on neutral territory and keep initial meetings brief and positive.

faqs.q: Do Field Spaniels bark a lot?
faqs.a: Field Spaniels are not considered excessive barkers. They may alert to strangers or unusual sounds, but are generally manageable with basic training. Consistent "quiet" reinforcement from puppyhood keeps this in check.

faqs.q: Are Field Spaniels good apartment dogs?
faqs.a: Field Spaniels can live in apartments if their exercise needs are met consistently. The key variable is owner commitment to daily walks and enrichment — breed size alone doesn't determine apartment suitability.

faqs.q: How much exercise does a Field Spaniel need per day?
faqs.a: Field Spaniels need approximately 45–60 minutes of exercise daily. A structured morning walk and an evening sniff walk usually cover their needs. Mental exercise (training sessions, puzzle feeders) counts toward overall stimulation needs and can reduce restless behaviour.

faqs.q: Are Field Spaniels good running partners?
faqs.a: Field Spaniels can join you for moderate runs once fully grown. They're better suited to steady 3–5 mile runs than extended distance. Watch for signs of fatigue and always run in cooler hours during summer.

faqs.q: What happens if a Field Spaniel doesn't get enough exercise?
faqs.a: Field Spaniels are less demanding than high-energy breeds, but chronic under-exercise still leads to weight gain and low-level restlessness. Even lower-energy breeds benefit from a consistent daily walk for both physical health and mental stimulation.

faqs.q: Can a Field Spaniel be off-lead?
faqs.a: Off-lead freedom for a Field Spaniel depends on recall reliability, not breed alone. Train recall from puppyhood using long-line sessions before progressing to full off-lead. A standard 20-foot long-line gives freedom while maintaining safety during the training phase.

faqs.q: How much should I feed my Field Spaniel?
faqs.a: A Field Spaniel needs approximately 1½–3 cups of dry food per day for an adult, split across two meals. Always follow the feeding guide on your specific formula — calorie density varies significantly between brands. Adjust portions based on body condition: you should be able to feel (but not easily see) the ribs.

faqs.q: How many times a day should I feed a Field Spaniel?
faqs.a: Adult Field Spaniels should eat twice daily. Puppies (under 6 months) need 3–4 smaller meals per day to support growth and prevent hypoglycaemia, particularly in small breeds.

faqs.q: What is the best food for a Field Spaniel?
faqs.a: Look for a formula carrying an AAFCO adequacy statement for the correct life stage. A named protein source (chicken, turkey, beef, salmon) should appear first in the ingredient list. Medium-energy Field Spaniels do well on standard adult maintenance formulas with named protein as the first ingredient.

faqs.q: When should I switch my Field Spaniel from puppy to adult food?
faqs.a: Most Field Spaniels can transition to adult food between 12 and 15 months. Transition gradually over 7–10 days — mix 25% new food with 75% old food and shift the ratio every 2 days to avoid digestive upset.

faqs.q: Is a Field Spaniel a good dog for first-time owners?
faqs.a: Field Spaniels are generally considered suitable for first-time owners. They're responsive to training, manageable in size, and adaptable to different home environments. A puppy class is still recommended to build a strong foundation.

faqs.q: Are Field Spaniels good family dogs?
faqs.a: Field Spaniels are typically affectionate family dogs that do well with children and adapt to household routines. Their sociable nature means they prefer company over isolation.

faqs.q: Do Field Spaniels do well when left alone?
faqs.a: Field Spaniels form strong bonds with their owners and do not do well with extended isolation. Aim for no more than 4–6 hours alone at a time. If your schedule requires longer absences, consider a dog walker, doggy daycare, or a companion dog.

faqs.q: How much time do you need for a Field Spaniel?
faqs.a: Plan for 1.5–2 hours per day dedicated to your Field Spaniel — covering exercise, training, feeding and general interaction. Add 15–30 minutes for grooming 3–4 times weekly. The commitment is consistent year-round, not just when convenient.
